transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I came in because I’ve been having a hard time caring about things I used to really enjoy. It’s probably not a huge deal, but… dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night with people I like—it all kind of feels like a chore now, like something I keep putting off. I don’t really feel like myself, if that makes sense.
Have you completely stopped enjoying those activities, or does it feel more like you just don’t care about them as much as you used to?

I wouldn’t say it’s completely gone, exactly… I mean, maybe if I actually went I might enjoy parts of it. But right now I barely care enough to start. Dance class, hiking, cooking, game night—things that used to feel like me—now they just kind of sit there like chores I keep putting off. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way about those activities?

Um… I guess it’s been a while. It started after the robbery at that festival job, about two years and three months ago. I don’t know if that’s the kind of timeline you mean, but… yeah, since then it’s just been different.
Has this loss of interest or enjoyment in activities you used to like affected other parts of your life beyond dance, hiking, cooking, and game nights?

Yeah… I think it has, a little. I mean, I’m still functioning, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve missed some Chamber application deadlines, and I keep putting my catering plans on hold. The paperwork and reaching out to people and lining up jobs just feels harder to manage than it used to.

And socially, I guess I see friends less. It’s not like I don’t like them anymore… I just keep choosing what feels easier or safer, and my life has gotten kind of smaller because of that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed feeling down or sad most days, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to say I’m sad all day every day, because that sounds dramatic and I do have okay moments. But most days there’s this kind of low feeling underneath everything… like a sour mix of being scared and guilty, even when nothing is actually happening.

I don’t always have a clear reason for it, which makes me feel kind of silly saying it. But it’s there a lot. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight since this started—like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual?

Um… not really, I don’t think. My appetite maybe goes up and down a little depending on the day, but I haven’t noticed anything major, like a big change in how much I eat or my weight.

I’m sorry, I know that’s not very specific. I just don’t think that’s been one of the bigger changes for me.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or having less energy than usual, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

I’m not sure… I don’t think it’s a huge thing for me. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of worn out, but I don’t know if that’s more than anyone would feel.

I haven’t really noticed a major drop in energy, at least not something I’d point to as one of the main problems. Is that okay to say?
Have you had trouble sleeping recently, like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early?

I don’t think so… not in a way that really stands out. I mean, I have the occasional night where it takes me a bit to settle, but I wouldn’t say I’m regularly not sleeping or waking up super early or anything like that.

I hope that makes sense. It just hasn’t felt like one of the main problems for me.
Have you ever felt so down or hopeless that you’ve thought about hurting yourself or ending your life?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt really overwhelmed sometimes, but I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself or ending my life.

I’m sorry, that’s a serious question—I just… I don’t think that’s been happening for me.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?

A little, yeah… I mean, not all the time, but I notice it when I’m trying to do paperwork. Like with catering forms or an application for the Chamber, I’ll read the same line over and over and it just doesn’t really stick.

And then I get kind of stuck on small decisions, like what price to put down or which email I should answer first. It feels silly saying it out loud, because it’s not like I can’t think at all, but… it does slow me down. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had these feelings of low mood and loss of interest almost every day for at least the last two years, or have there been significant periods where you felt better?

Um… yeah, I guess it’s been around since that robbery at the festival job. That was about two years and three months ago now.

I don’t know if I’d say it’s been exactly the same every single day, but it hasn’t really gone back to how I was before. There have been better stretches, sure, but… overall, since then, it’s kind of been there. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Would you say that you’ve completely stopped getting pleasure from most things, or does it feel like you just get less pleasure from them than you used to?

I wouldn’t say completely stopped, exactly… I can still sometimes think, “Oh, that used to be fun,” but it just doesn’t pull me in like it used to.

Like dance class, hiking, trying a new recipe, even game night… those were things that made me feel like myself. Now they kind of sit there like chores I keep putting off. So I guess it’s less pleasure, but pretty noticeably less. Does that make sense?
Would you say that most days, your mood feels depressed or down for most of the day, even if it’s not extremely intense?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I can still get through the day, but most days there’s this… heaviness, I guess.

It’s not always like crying or anything. It’s more like this low, sour feeling under everything—fear and guilt mixed together—even when nothing bad is actually happening. It’s just kind of there in the background a lot of the day.

Is that what you mean by depressed or down?
Would you say that you’ve felt a noticeable loss of energy or a lot more fatigue most days, even when you’re not doing anything particularly tiring?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that from just… being unmotivated, I guess.

I do feel worn out more than I used to, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s a huge fatigue thing every day. Some days I can get things done okay, and other days even small stuff feels like it takes more out of me than it should. Is that the kind of energy you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight since this started—like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Um… not really that I’ve noticed. I mean, my eating probably isn’t perfect or anything, but I don’t think there’s been a big change like suddenly eating a lot more or a lot less.

And my weight seems pretty much the same, as far as I can tell. I haven’t been tracking it closely, though—is that okay to say?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most activities you used to enjoy, to the point where almost nothing really feels worth the effort?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair. I mean, I don’t want to say nothing matters, because that sounds worse than I mean it, but… a lot of the things that used to make me feel like myself just don’t pull me in anymore.

Like dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, game night… I used to actually look forward to that stuff. Now it kind of just sits there like a chore I keep putting off. Even when I know I might feel better if I went, it feels like too much effort to care, if that makes sense.

Would you say that, for most of the time over the past two years, you've felt down or lost interest in almost everything for most of the day, even if there were short breaks where you felt a little better?

I’m not sure about the “most of the time over two years” part exactly… I don’t want to overstate it. But the reason I came in is that I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself.

Like dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night… they all just kind of sit there now like chores I keep putting off. So, yeah, the lost interest part is definitely there. I just don’t know if I’m answering the timeframe part correctly.
